coords: font units; x from the word origin (the element's left edge), y down from the baseline (ascenders negative). Each letter's d and bbox [x0, y0, x1, y1] are relative to its own origin: place it at translate(left + x*s, baseline) scale(s), s = fontSize/unitsPerEm.
shaping: cmap, GSUB ccmp/liga/calt (ff becomes the f_f ligature: one letter with char "ff"), GPOS kern pairs (kern = extra advance after the letter, already in the next x). Chrome drops liga when letter-spacing is not 0: then ff is two f's and these x values no longer hold.
baseline: baseline = top + floor((L - (A + D)) / 2) + A, A = round(965*s), D = round(235*s) (halves up), s = fontSize/1000, L = used line-height, top = the element's content-box top, all in CSS px (also at devicePixelRatio 2). Chrome paints the glyphs at round(baseline), a whole CSS px, and they come out about 1/4 device px higher than the exact outline. 600 120px/1.12: baseline = top + 111.
drips: first letter only: lowest points of its bottom outline (feet, bottom curves), tangent pointing right and outward normal, y down. landing: top of its first stroke from the left.

check.how: Chrome (Playwright) at dpr 1 and 2. words: Chrome text minus our paths at 600 120px/1.12, px, phase correlation; inkDiff = share of ink that differs (antialiasing). probes: Chrome's line baseline (an empty inline-block on it) vs the formula, and the painted offset of "Nom" from the formula's baseline, before and after snapping that to a whole CSS px.
